Build the complex survey design for BDHS data

Source: R/design.R
bdhs_design.Rd

Creates a survey::svydesign() object with the clustering, stratification and weights that the DHS Program uses for the given recode, so standard errors and confidence intervals are correct. The round and recode are detected automatically for data read with bdhs_read() or bdhs_simulate(). bdhs_design_info() documents the design of every round.

Usage

bdhs_design(
  data,
  weight = "default",
  strata = c("auto", "design", "region_residence", "none"),
  survey = NULL,
  recode = NULL,
  srvyr = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of BDHS recode data (one round, or several rounds pooled with bdhs_pool()).

weight

Which weight to use.

  • "default": pool_wt for pooled data made by bdhs_pool(), otherwise the standard weight of the recode (v005 for women, children and births, hv005 for households and members, mv005 for men).

  • "dv": the domestic violence module weight (d005; md005 for men).

  • "male": the household weight for the men's subsample (hv028) in household and member files; mv005 in the men's file.

  • "household": the household weight hv005.

  • A column name. DHS weights with six implied decimals (*005, hv028, ha69, hb69) are divided by 1e6.

strata

Stratification. "auto" (default) uses the DHS sampling-error strata (v022/hv022/mv022), which is the DHS Program's recommendation for variance estimation. "design" uses v023, and "region_residence" uses region x urban/rural. "none" ignores stratification (not recommended).

survey, recode

Optional explicit survey and recode, overriding detection.

srvyr

If TRUE, return a tbl_svy object for use with the srvyr package.

Value

A survey.design2 object (or a tbl_svy when srvyr = TRUE) with attributes bdhs_survey_id, bdhs_recode, bdhs_weight (the weight column used) and bdhs_singleton_strata (number of strata with one PSU).

Details

Pooled data (several rounds, see bdhs_pool()) get round-specific PSU and strata identifiers, and the pooled weight pool_wt is used when present.

Some strata can contain a single PSU (for example after subsetting, or in small domains). The variance of such strata cannot be estimated with the default options(survey.lonely.psu = "fail"); bdhs_design() tells you once per session when this happens. The usual fix, used by the DHS Program's own software (centering at the grand mean), is options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust").

Examples

ir <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "IR")
des <- bdhs_design(ir)
survey::svymean(~v201, des)
#>        mean     SE
#> v201 3.5713 0.1092

# Pooled rounds: round-specific strata and PSUs, pooled weights
p <- bdhs_pool(bdhs_simulate(2017, "IR"), bdhs_simulate(2022, "IR"))
#> ℹ Value labels differ between rounds for 3 columns; kept the codes and dropped
#>   the labels: `v022`, `v023`, and `v024`.
#> ℹ DHS codes are not always comparable across rounds; use `harmonize = TRUE` or
#>   `bdhs_harmonize()` for comparable variables.
survey::svyby(~v201, ~survey_id, bdhs_design(p), survey::svymean)
#>           survey_id     v201        se
#> BD2017DHS BD2017DHS 3.420633 0.1107607
#> BD2022DHS BD2022DHS 3.571310 0.1091613
